name: lance_file::versions::v1::reader::FileReader::try_new_with_fragment_id
behavior: Public traced try_new_with_fragment_id opens the ObjectStore path, loads metadata, then forwards the supplied Schema, u32 fragment ID, signed min/max field bounds and optional LanceCache to try_new_from_reader with Some(metadata). No schema/dictionary hydration is performed here. Docs mention an optional manifest and row-ID high bits, but the actual signature requires Schema and this file emits no row IDs. IO/cache errors propagate before reader construction.
callers: FileReader::try_new; Dataset fragment legacy open and local projection fixture.
callees: ObjectStore::open; read_metadata; try_new_from_reader.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::reader::FileReader::try_new_from_reader
behavior: Public try_new_from_reader accepts an arbitrary Arc<dyn Reader>, separate Path, optional Arc<Metadata>, supplied Schema and cache/bounds. Some metadata is trusted directly; None calls read_metadata. No equality check relates the separate path to object_reader.path, the metadata to the file, bounds to schema, or the schema dictionary values to file contents. Ordinary PageTable loading uses the separately supplied path string as cache key and metadata.page_table_position, signed field bounds and num_batches cast to i32. Statistics loading uses object_reader and its own path. try_join polls both table futures concurrently; first error prevents constructing Self, with no local task spawn/abort or rollback. Statistics loading calls read_metadata independently, so a supplied metadata Arc does not eliminate that read; without cache the ordinary open path can load metadata twice. Successful construction retains all supplied/shared values and widens fragment ID to u64.
callers: try_new_with_fragment_id; table SelfDescribingFileReader implementation; Dataset write fixture.
callees: read_metadata optionally; load_from_cache; PageTable::load; read_stats_page_table; futures::try_join.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::reader::FileReader::read_metadata
behavior: Public read_metadata caches by object_reader.path string. On miss: await size, read min(size,block_size) tail, decode the metadata position, then either read_struct at an earlier location or slice the tail and decode in memory. It does not validate footer magic/version or schema here. read_metadata_offset only checks tail length>=16 and extracts LEu64; read_struct_from_buf trusts the u32 length while slicing. Out-of-file offsets, short/malformed tail bodies and arithmetic are not locally guarded and can panic before structured decoding errors (rust/lance-io/src/utils.rs:221-231; rust/lance-io/src/utils.rs:248-263). Earlier-position read_struct uses its separate framed IO path.
callers: Constructors, statistics loader, table SelfDescribingFileReader.
callees: load_from_cache; Reader::size/block_size/get_range; read_metadata_offset; read_struct/read_struct_from_buf.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::reader::FileReader::read_stats_page_table
behavior: Private read_stats_page_table caches Option<PageTable> under reader.path joined with stats, including None. Its loader obtains metadata again and, when stats_metadata exists, loads one batch with field bounds0..max(leaf_field_ids). Empty leaf IDs panic at max().unwrap; no schema/presence/table consistency validation is added. Statistics and ordinary tables use distinct value types in addition to different path strings.
callers: try_new_from_reader.
callees: load_from_cache; read_metadata; max leaf ID; PageTable::load.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::reader::FileReader::load_from_cache
behavior: Generic async load_from_cache requires DeepSizeOf+Send+Sync+StableStringCacheValue and a Send+Sync Fn loader returning a Send future. Some cache delegates get_or_insert_with_key using borrowed StringCacheKey; no-cache awaits the loader and wraps the result in Arc. The owned key String remains alive through the await. No local expiration, persistence codec, invalidation, file identity verification or duplicate-load policy is added beyond the chosen cache implementation.
callers: Metadata and both page-table loading paths.
callees: StringCacheKey::new; LanceCache::get_or_insert_with_key or direct loader await.

Private io_parallelism returns the Reader policy unchanged, with no zero-value clamp or local override.
callers: Local reader/writer/compatibility fixtures and public frozen reader API.
callees: Schema::max_field_id; try_new_with_fragment_id with zero IDs and no cache.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::reader::FileReader::read_batch
behavior: Public instrumented method read_batch converts params to ReadBatchParams then calls the free read_batch with the explicit projection. Its doc says returned schema is FileReader::schema(), but actual output follows the projection argument; there is no subset/type/field-ID validation against self.schema at this boundary.
callers: read_range, take, batches_stream and fixtures.
callees: Free read_batch after parameter conversion.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::reader::FileReader::read_range
behavior: Public read_range returns a typed empty RecordBatch for every Range::is_empty before metadata/bounds checks, including reversed or beyond-end empty ranges. Nonempty ranges use metadata.range_to_batches, read batches with ordered buffered(reader parallelism), and collect all into Vec. A single batch returns a cheap clone; multiple batches concatenate in spawn_blocking with JoinError and Arrow error propagated. The code indexes batches[0] without guarding an unexpectedly empty split. No abort-on-drop handle is retained for blocking work.
callers: Public reader API and local range fixture.
callees: Metadata::range_to_batches; method read_batch; ordered buffered collection; spawn_blocking concat_batches.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::reader::FileReader::take
behavior: Public take documents sorted indices, but metadata.group_indices_to_batches clones and sorts them, retaining duplicates and discarding original unsorted order (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:128-163). Grouping happens before validation and assumes valid cumulative metadata. Each group rejects batch_id>=num_batches, then compares last local offset strictly greater than whole-file len cast to u32, not the selected batch length; codec checks supply additional bounds. Nonempty groups are assumed by expect. Ordered buffered reads collect all batches, then spawn_blocking concat even for zero/one group using the requested schema. No output reorder restores caller order; empty take performs no per-column read.
callers: Public reader API and numeric/list/Boolean fixtures.
callees: Metadata::group_indices_to_batches; method read_batch; ordered buffered collection; spawn_blocking concat_batches.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::reader::FileReader::page_stats_schema
behavior: page_stats_schema returns None only when stats metadata is absent. Otherwise parse each root statistics field name as i32, retain roots whose parsed data-field ID occurs in requested IDs, append that root ID plus immediate child IDs, then project_by_ids(include children=true). Unparseable names and missing requested IDs are silently skipped; results follow statistics schema order, not caller order, with linear contains lookup. An existing stats schema can yield Some(empty schema).
callers: read_page_stats and public reader API.
callees: Parse statistics root names; Schema::project_by_ids.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::reader::FileReader::read_page_stats
behavior: read_page_stats returns None when the cached optional statistics table is absent. If present, it unwraps page_stats_schema, returns None for an empty projection, otherwise reads selected root fields at batch0/RangeFull using the stats table with ordered buffered parallelism. It collects every array and constructs one RecordBatch. A supplied-metadata versus independently loaded stats-table disagreement can make the unwrap panic; statistics fields are not cross-validated here.
callers: Public statistics API; complete Dataset/statistics consumer graph pending.
callees: page_stats_schema; read_array with statistics table and batch0; RecordBatch::try_new.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::reader::batches_stream
behavior: Public batches_stream consumes FileReader, Schema and a mutable Send+Sync static batch-ID predicate. It snapshots num_batches as i32, lazily filters IDs in increasing order, retains reader/projection in Arcs and reads whole batches with fixed buffered(2), independent of Reader io_parallelism for this outer layer. The stream adapter advertises the supplied projection schema; each batch may still perform parallel field reads. No Tokio task is spawned here despite thread-sharing comments; dropping the stream drops pending local futures, without a backend cancellation guarantee.
callers: Local even-batch stream fixture and public frozen API.
callees: FileReader::num_batches/read_batch; predicate; buffered(2); RecordBatchStreamAdapter.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::reader::read_batch
behavior: Public free read_batch rejects an empty schema with InvalidInput no fields requested. Its comment about with_row_id and panic is stale: no such flag or row-ID synthesis exists. Nonempty roots are read concurrently via ordered buffered(reader parallelism), collected, then RecordBatch::try_new checks assembled arrays against converted explicit schema. No upfront batch-ID validation occurs; missing page errors or codec errors emerge during reads.
callers: FileReader method; Dataset fragment ranges_to_tasks.
callees: read_array over roots; ordered buffered collection; RecordBatch::try_new or InvalidInput.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::reader::read_array
behavior: Private async-recursive read_array reconstructs field.data_type and first routes is_fixed_stride to plain decoding. Otherwise handles Null, four binary/string families, Struct, Dictionary, List<Int32 offsets> and LargeList<Int64 offsets>. Other types panic via unimplemented rather than returning NotSupported. In the locally read predicate every FSL is fixed-stride, regardless of child; Interval has byte_width support but is absent from is_fixed_stride, so predicate/type-dispatch differences matter (rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:111-181). No field.encoding tag drives this dispatch.
callers: Free read_batch, statistics reads, struct/list recursion and null fixture helper.
callees: DataTypeExt::is_fixed_stride; fixed/null/binary/dictionary/struct/list adapters.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::reader::get_page_info
behavior: get_page_info looks up exact signed field.id and batch_id in the provided PageTable. Missing entry becomes InvalidInput with field name, field ID and batch ID. It performs no file-bound or length validation on the returned PageInfo.
callers: Fixed/null/binary/dictionary/list adapters.
callees: PageTable::get; contextual InvalidInput.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::reader::_read_fixed_stride_array
behavior: _read_fixed_stride_array fetches page info from its supplied table, reconstructs field DataType and forwards position, length and cloned selector to the V1 facade. It passes neither field.nullable nor a separate validity bitmap; plain codec semantics govern primitive/fixed-array null handling.
callers: read_array fixed-stride branch.
callees: get_page_info; encoding::read_fixed_stride_array.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::reader::read_null_array
behavior: read_null_array obtains page info but performs no payload IO. Empty Indices produces0; nonempty raw indices.values determines maximum, rejecting max>=page length, then uses indices.len. Index validity is ignored, so null selector backing values participate in bounds checks and every selector slot counts as a Null output row. For null ranges, derive start/end for Range/full/to/from, reject only end>page length, then subtract start from end unchecked. Reversed ranges or RangeFrom beyond length can underflow rather than following PlainDecoder empty-range behavior. Ranges reaches unreachable!, not InvalidInput. Finally allocate a NullArray of the computed count. The inline wrap comment adds no behavior.
callers: read_array Null branch.
callees: get_page_info; selector bounds; NullArray::new.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::reader::read_binary_array

name: lance_file::versions::v1::reader::take_list_array
behavior: Generic take_list_array expects a nonempty sorted UInt32 selector. It subtracts the first selector from every raw selector value and indexes the already fetched position span to create per-list child ranges. Null selector validity is ignored, and unsigned subtraction, positions and first-child existence are unchecked. It clones the Field and accumulates arrays rather than streaming child values. For each selected list range, await read_array on children[0] sequentially, so repeated indices cause repeated child reads at this layer. Retain all arrays, build offsets from summed range lengths with unchecked addition/conversion, concatenate all values, and build a generic list. No separate list validity is restored; the helper creates an all-valid List/LargeList with child named item and nullable=true from the actual value type (rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:202-229). This does not preserve arbitrary original child metadata or nullability.
callers: read_list_array Indices branch.
callees: Per-selector child ranges; sequential read_array; concat; primitive offset builder; try_new_generic_list_array.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::reader::read_list_array
behavior: read_list_array expands Range end and RangeTo end by1 for the terminal offset; Indices reads the entire first..last+2 position interval. RangeFull/from pass through unchanged. Empty direct Indices panics at first/last access before page lookup; no sorting or validity checks are local. Arithmetic is unchecked. Multiple Ranges is initially passed through to fixed-stride decoding. List position lookup deliberately uses reader.page_table rather than the page_table argument, then reads T::DATA_TYPE (Int32/Int64) with the PageInfo position and length. Children later use the supplied table. This distinction matters if invoked with a statistics or other alternate table; no local assertion ensures equality. The position result is downcast to the generic primitive type. Map logical list selectors to child rows: Range uses first and range-length endpoint; To uses0..positions[end]; From uses first position..child end; Full uses first..last position; Indices returns take_list_array. Ranges has an Internal error branch, but ordinary fixed-stride decoding rejects that selector earlier. Position access, range subtraction and child bounds are delegated/unchecked rather than preflighted. Subtract first absolute position from all offsets with Arrow arithmetic, recursively read children[0] over derived child selector using the supplied page table, and call try_new_generic_list_array. Parent validity and original child field metadata are not passed. Arrow arithmetic/building errors propagate; no local offset monotonicity, nonnegativity or payload-length check precedes them.
callers: read_array List/LargeList branch.
callees: get_page_info on reader ordinary table; fixed-stride positions; take_list_array or recursive read_array; Arrow sub; try_new_generic_list_array.
